title: Advancing The CFET-Based Device Roadmap: Novel Integration Modules And Standard Cell Configurations
gist: Part 2 of imec's CFET roadmap article: a double-flip sequential CFET (sCFET) reaches 98% library efficiency and enables 3T cells with both split-gate and common-gate options, a 5T+1 CFET SRAM bit cell is 12.5% smaller than a 6T CFET cell with 7-15% faster write, and raising the metal-1 gear ratio to 2:1 (needing single-patterning High NA EUV) improves A7 BEOL routability.

insights.claim: From the A7 logic node onward the industry may transition to CFET transistors, which stack p and nMOS devices to shrink standard cells to 3T and extend the CMOS logic roadmap to at least A3, while GAA nanosheets scale to A10 with 5.5T cells.
insights.speaker: Geert Hellings
insights.so_what: Defines the device-architecture sequence (FinFET, nanosheet, CFET) that sets multi-year capex and tooling demand for foundries and equipment makers.
insights.quote: From the A7 logic technology node onwards, industry may likely transition to CFET-based transistor architectures

insights.claim: For A7 imec offers alternatives to CFET: its CMOS 2.0 paradigm that partitions an SoC into heterogeneous tiers connected with 3D interconnects, or pushing GAA nanosheets to their limits with frontside or backside power delivery.
insights.speaker: Geert Hellings
insights.so_what: CFET is not the only A7 path, so adoption timing is uncertain; watch which route leading foundries pick.
insights.locator: For the A7 node, options are becoming increasingly diverse

insights.claim: Monolithic CFET (mCFET) is believed to offer the fastest path to industrial adoption pending better alignment accuracy in sequential CFET, because sCFET requires two wafer flips that distort the wafer and challenge front-to-back alignment.
insights.speaker: Geert Hellings
insights.so_what: The adoption risk for sCFET is wafer-flip alignment; mCFET is the base case for first production.
insights.quote: Pending further progress in alignment accuracy, mCFET is believed to offer the fastest path to industrial adoption.

insights.claim: Imec’s work is carried out in the European NanoIC pilot line, funded by the Chips Joint Undertaking, the EU Digital Europe and Horizon Europe programs and several member states, and targets beyond-2nm systems-on-chip so Europe stays at the forefront of next-generation manufacturing.
insights.speaker: Geert Hellings
insights.so_what: Public funding underpins Europe’s CFET R&D position versus US, Asian and Taiwanese leaders.

insights.claim: mCFET naturally yields common-gate devices, which suit 90-95% of basic logic gates, but flip-flops and multiplexers need independent n and p gates, and the workaround of leaving one polarity unused wastes the area benefit of stacking.
insights.speaker: Geert Hellings
insights.so_what: Explains the design-technology gap that split-gate sCFET is built to fill.

insights.claim: Imec’s double-flip sCFET (2026 VLSI) offers both split-gate and common-gate options without area penalty, reaching up to 98% overall library efficiency, higher than double-row and half-height double-row mCFET, and with dense backside metal-0 supports the 3T cells needed for A3 and A2.
insights.speaker: Geert Hellings
insights.so_what: Raises the scaling ceiling for sCFET and suggests the path to A3/A2 logic, relevant for the leading-edge foundry roadmap.
insights.quote: overall library efficiency (h) as high as 98%

insights.claim: Hybrid channels with different channel orientation or asymmetric sheet widths for top and bottom devices offer further power-performance-area gains and design flexibility for CFETs.
insights.speaker: Geert Hellings
insights.so_what: An extra scaling booster beyond A7; adds process complexity.

insights.claim: SRAM bit cell scaling has fallen flat relative to logic scaling since the 7nm node, and even GAA-nanosheet 6T SRAM did not deliver required power, performance and area benefits.
insights.speaker: Geert Hellings
insights.so_what: SRAM density stagnation caps on-chip cache and AI chip area scaling; a key bottleneck for cost-per-bit economics at advanced nodes.
insights.quote: since the 7nm technology node, SRAM bit cell scaling has fallen flat compared to logic CMOS device scaling

insights.claim: A 6T SRAM maps poorly onto CFET because the two pass-gate nFETs leave the top p-type devices unused, so CFET’s vertical density advantage does not translate into bit cell area, and a plain 5T cell has writability and noise problems.
insights.speaker: Geert Hellings
insights.so_what: Explains why simply moving to CFET does not fix SRAM scaling.
insights.locator: But even in the CFET SRAM era

insights.claim: Imec’s 5T+1 CFET SRAM replaces the two pass gates with one CFET transmission gate (an nFET plus pFET with independent gate control from split-gate sCFET), keeping a 5T footprint, improving writability, giving a 12.5% smaller bit cell than a 6T CFET SRAM and 7-15% faster write.
insights.speaker: Geert Hellings
insights.so_what: A concrete route to prolong SRAM scaling toward A7 and beyond; relevant to cache-heavy AI and CPU designs.
insights.quote: 12.5% smaller bit cell compared to a conventional 6T CFET SRAM cell, with 7-15% faster write operation

insights.claim: Starting from the 2nm node, contact poly pitch and metal-1 pitch scaling have slowed, increasing frontside routing congestion and limiting access to standard-cell pins, so standard-cell area gains from CFET can be undone by BEOL interconnect problems.
insights.speaker: Geert Hellings
insights.so_what: Interconnect, not transistors, may be the scaling limiter in the angstrom era, shifting value to routing, lithography and backside metallization.
insights.quote: the area advantages at standard cell level can easily be undone by scaling issues in the BEOL

insights.claim: Raising the gear ratio (CPP to metal-1 pitch) from about 1:1 typical at 2nm to 2:1 for A7 CFET designs improves pin accessibility and area utilization without hurting power or performance, but requires smaller metal-1 pitches that need single-patterning High NA EUV lithography.
insights.speaker: Geert Hellings
insights.so_what: Ties CFET scaling to High NA EUV adoption, supporting ASML-linked demand at A7.
